lessons.title: Matrices acting on vectors
lessons.purpose: Read matrix dimensions and apply a small matrix to a column vector.
lessons.scope: Rows, columns, dimensions and entry notation; matrix-vector multiplication as a weighted combination of columns; identity and zero matrices; plane scaling, reflection and shear.
lessons.boundary: No abstract basis theory or eigenvectors. Use explicit coordinate geometry; dimensions must be compatible.
lessons.practiceAndEvidence: Calculate transformed points/vectors and predict basic shapes; identify columns from the images of coordinate unit vectors; diagnose a dimension mismatch.
lessons.visualPlan: Coordinate grid before/after reflection and shear with labelled basis arrows.
lessons.handover: L02 composes these transformations; L03 reuses matrix notation for coupled equations.

lessons.title: Composing transformations in order
externalRequires: P101 U01 programming readiness as specified at U02-L05.
lessons.purpose: Compute a product of two small matrices and relate order to successive transformations.
lessons.scope: Derive the 2-by-2 product from successive matrix-vector application; rightmost transformation acts first; contrast a noncommuting pair with identity and a simple commuting pair.
lessons.boundary: Do not generalise noncommutativity to a claim that every pair fails to commute. No general rotation-angle formula or new trigonometry syllabus.
lessons.practiceAndEvidence: Calculate a shear/reflection composition both ways, compare on coordinate vectors and an independent vector; hand-trace and run a supplied short scalar/list function.
lessons.visualPlan: Two transformation paths from the same starting figure, with intermediate states.
lessons.python: 0.5 hour included: reuse P101 functions/lists to compare successive applications with the hand-computed product; no matrix library.
lessons.handover: L03–L04 solve coupled equations; L05 returns to reversible and collapsed transformations.

lessons.title: Solving simultaneous equations by elimination
lessons.purpose: Solve small coupled linear equations using justified elimination and check against the original equations.
lessons.scope: Translate supplied relationships into a system; equation and augmented-matrix forms; reversible elementary row operations; two unknowns first and one guided three-unknown example; back substitution.
lessons.boundary: No general-purpose algorithm implementation or unqualified division by a coefficient that may be zero. Introduce row exchange explicitly.
lessons.practiceAndEvidence: Move from worked to partially completed to independent two-unknown systems; carry out a guided three-unknown solution; substitute into every original equation and explain preservation of solutions.
lessons.visualPlan: Aligned equations and row operations; intersecting lines for the two-unknown case.
lessons.handover: L04 handles cases in which elimination does not produce one unique answer; L06 samples independent reasoning.

lessons.title: When solutions fail or are not unique
lessons.purpose: Classify unique, inconsistent and dependent small systems and represent a simple solution family.
lessons.scope: Contradiction versus redundant equation after elimination; parallel/coincident lines; a free parameter in a dependent two-unknown system; interpret a parameterised family by substitution.
lessons.boundary: No rank theorem or abstract null spaces. A singular coefficient matrix alone cannot distinguish no solutions from infinitely many.
lessons.practiceAndEvidence: Classify deliberately similar systems with different right-hand sides; show one inconsistent and one dependent case; check two members of a solution family and explain why examples alone do not describe the whole family.
lessons.visualPlan: Intersecting, parallel and coincident line pairs aligned with their reduced equations.
lessons.handover: L05 connects 2D invertibility and determinant with this distinction.

lessons.title: Determinants, invertibility and computational checks
externalRequires: P101 U01 programming readiness as specified at U02-L05.
lessons.purpose: Interpret a 2-by-2 determinant and validate transformation and solution calculations transparently.
lessons.scope: ad−bc, signed area scale and collapse in 2D; determinant nonzero as the invertibility condition; obtain/check a simple inverse by reversing a transformation or solving for its columns; substitute hand solutions into original systems.
lessons.boundary: No 3-by-3 determinant expansion, general inverse algorithm or eigenmethods. Coding checks a supplied candidate, not an automatic solver. A zero residual is not evidence of uniqueness.
lessons.practiceAndEvidence: Use contrasting invertible and singular integer matrices; compare transformed unit-square area with determinant; write a 2-by-2 transformation function and residual calculation; test a valid, invalid and dependent-system candidate. Explain each check’s limits.
lessons.visualPlan: Unit square transformed into parallelogram or collapsed line, with orientation clearly labelled.
lessons.python: 2 hours included: independently implement a fixed small matrix-vector calculation and residual check with lists/functions, explain results and rerun cleanly. No solver, arrays or plotting required.
lessons.handover: L06 integrates O4/O6 evidence; M102 will extend bases, orthogonality and eigenmethods.

lessons.title: Block synthesis, iCMA 01 and unit review
externalRequires: P101 U01 programming readiness as specified at U02-L05.
lessons.purpose: Connect vector, transformation and equation methods and prepare for TMA 01 using formative evidence.
lessons.scope: Interleaved block practice, one short code interpretation/correction, embedded iCMA 01 and explanatory feedback; U03 reference table/PDF; assess readiness for the separately budgeted TMA.
lessons.boundary: No new content, additional graded assignment, invented pass threshold or claim of mastery. iCMA is formative; TMA questions and marking guide remain to be authored.
lessons.practiceAndEvidence: Use 1 hour of retrieval/feedback for iCMA attempt plus feedback and targeted correction, and 0.5 hour for the unit reference-sheet review. Mixed practice samples vector signs/products, composition order and system classification; the code check asks what it cannot establish.
lessons.visualPlan: Concise decision diagram connecting representation, method and independent check.
lessons.python: 0.5 hour included: interpret and repair a short scalar/list residual check, using already taught syntax.
lessons.handover: TMA 01 follows with its existing separate 6 hours and O3/O4/O6 remit. B02 U04 retrieves algebra/functions; M102 extends linear algebra after relevant readiness.
